claim: The majority relied on Section 6(g) of the FTC Act as its source of authority, but the dissenters argued that Section 6(g) only authorizes procedural or internal operating rules, not substantive legal rules carrying the force of law
evidence: based on the text and structure of the FTC Act, I am persuaded that a reviewing court would interpret Section 6(g) to authorize only procedural or internal operating rules, not substantive legal rules.
excerpt: The Commission asserts that Section 5’s authority regarding unfair methods of competition works together with Section 6(g) to permit the Commission to promulgate competition rules. 16 But, as further explained below, based on the text and structure of the FTC Act, I am persuaded that a reviewing court would interpret Section 6(g) to authorize only procedural or internal operating rules, not substantive legal rules. 17 The Commission thus cannot rely on 6(g) to promulgate competition legislative rules.
